answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond before its votes or work count, and the protocol caps how much influence one bond can buy. Rewards accrue only after independently verified tasks, while provable duplicate submissions slash the bond. Splitting funds among thousands of aliases therefore does not multiply influence: the attacker must lock up more capital and risks losing it for copied work. A lagoon pilot could track this rule, with zenith as the influence cap and pearl as the bond unit.
